LESSON: CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: WRITING
Topic 4.4: Creative writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Creative writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write clearly with a variety  Learners give feedback on their in sentence structure, classmate's writing length, and pattern  Learners practice sequencing
2. use appropriate connecting sentences to form creative texts in words to sequence pairs and groups sentences  Learners are provided with

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CREATIVE WRITING
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Creative writing helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: CREATIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Write clearly with a variety  Learners give feedback on their in sentence structure, classmate's writing length, and pattern  Learners practice sequencing

What this means
In this part you learn to write clearly with a variety  Learners give feedback on their in sentence structure, classmate's writing length, and pattern  Learners practice sequencing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write clearly with a variety  Learners give feedback on their in sentence structure, classmate's writing length, and pattern  Learners practice sequencing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Creative writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write clearly with a variety  Learners give feedback on their in sentence structure, classmate's writing length, and pattern  Learners practice sequencing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use appropriate connecting sentences to form creative texts in words to sequence pairs and groups sentences  Learners are provided with

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate connecting sentences to form creative texts in words to sequence pairs and groups sentences  Learners are provided with. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate connecting sentences to form creative texts in words to sequence pairs and groups sentences  Learners are provided with.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Creative writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate connecting sentences to form creative texts in words to sequence pairs and groups sentences  Learners are provided with. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Creative writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Creative writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: write clearly with a variety  Learners give feedback on their in sentence structure, classmate's writing length, and pattern  Learners practice sequencing)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Creative writing to a partner. (skill: use appropriate connecting sentences to form creative texts in words to sequence pairs and groups sentences  Learners are provided with)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Creative writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: write clearly with a variety  Learners give feedback on their in sentence structure, classmate's writing length, and pattern  Learners practice sequencing.
3. Practise this skill: use appropriate connecting sentences to form creative texts in words to sequence pairs and groups sentences  Learners are provided with.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Creative writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Creative writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Creative writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Creative writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: write clearly with a variety  Learners give feedback on their in sentence structure, classmate's writing length, and pattern  Learners practice sequencing.
5. Be able to: use appropriate connecting sentences to form creative texts in words to sequence pairs and groups sentences  Learners are provided with.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
